memory_update.text: AXTI should be prioritized in later layers as the most direct US-listed InP substrate chokepoint candidate; key survival tests are export-permit cadence, customer backlog quality, 6-inch InP qualification, and Tongmei capacity ramp.
VECO is a second-order InP capacity-build beneficiary with unusually clean evidence from a May 2026 order announcement tied to InP laser manufacturing tools.
POET belongs in a speculative-shadow lane, not the core substrate lane, unless later evidence proves material InP efficiency gains, qualified volume shipments, and reliable InP laser-die supply.
The node should be tracked across three sublayers: InP substrates, InP laser/device fab capacity, and integration/packaging architectures that affect effective InP utilization.

Need deeper verification of non-US-listed dominant substrate suppliers Sumitomo Electric and JX Advanced Metals/JX Nippon as competitive context, even though this pass is limited to US-listed candidates.

node: Indium phosphide wafers and optical-interconnect substrates
summary: Layer 1B expansion found one unusually direct underfollowed public substrate candidate, AXTI, plus one underfollowed equipment beneficiary, VECO, one speculative photonic-integration efficiency play, POET, and one large-cap reference anchor, COHR. The strongest direct chokepoint mapping is AXTI because it discloses InP substrate production, China-linked export-permit risk, and capacity-expansion financing. VECO is a second-order bottleneck supplier because its tools are explicitly ordered for InP laser manufacturing. POET is not a substrate producer but may become relevant if its wafer-level optical interposer/light-source approach improves effective InP utilization. COHR is included only as a reference leader/context anchor for vertically integrated InP optical devices and AI datacenter demand pull-through.
